account: On 23 April 2026, Professor Xu Huizhuo's team implanted the IMIE intelligent retina in a 61-year-old woman known as Auntie Chen. The team is at Xiangya Hospital, Central South University, Changsha. The implant is a 256-channel epiretinal array driven by camera glasses and an external video processor. She was diagnosed with retinitis pigmentosa at 40 and had been blind for over ten years. Mark Humayun advised in the operating room, and no serious complications occurred. On 5 June 2026, the hospital announced that after over a month of rehabilitation she could identify E optotypes (acuity 0.03, peak 0.1). She could also walk indoors and through doorways without an escort. She is the first subject of a Phase I trial. The team says that she lacks full self-care ability and that she will be observed for a year. In a review published on 27 July 2026, researchers at Ewha Womans University wrote that IMIE 256 remains an early-stage clinical platform. They said that long-term adoption, multicenter validation and definitive regulatory translation have not been established. Their review covers the 2021 results and does not discuss the 2026 Xiangya case.

ai_role.statement: The system is the whole substitute visual pathway. Camera glasses capture the scene. An external processor converts each frame in real time into stimulation patterns across 256 electrodes. The implant stimulates surviving ganglion cells whose signals reach the visual cortex. The patient had no vision before, so the benefit is attributable to the system together with structured rehabilitation. The 2026 reports describe the conversion only as an algorithm inside an “intelligent” retina. The 2021 IMIE 256 paper describes a video processing unit with a per-electrode threshold map and 15 gray levels and no learned model. How much of that processing is AI in a machine-learning sense is not established by these sources.

fields.account: On 23 April 2026, Professor Xu Huizhuo's team implanted the IMIE intelligent retina in a 61-year-old woman known as Auntie Chen. The team is at Xiangya Hospital, Central South University, Changsha. The implant is a 256-channel epiretinal array driven by camera glasses and an external video processor. She was diagnosed with retinitis pigmentosa at 40 and had been blind for over ten years. Mark Humayun advised in the operating room, and no serious complications occurred. On 5 June 2026, the hospital announced that after over a month of rehabilitation she could identify E optotypes (acuity 0.03, peak 0.1). She could also walk indoors and through doorways without an escort. She is the first subject of a Phase I trial. The team says that she lacks full self-care ability and that she will be observed for a year. In a review published on 27 July 2026, researchers at Ewha Womans University wrote that IMIE 256 remains an early-stage clinical platform. They said that long-term adoption, multicenter validation and definitive regulatory translation have not been established. Their review covers the 2021 results and does not discuss the 2026 Xiangya case.
